title.en: Plants and animals in different surroundings, and the importance of habitat

text.en:
A camel in the desert and a penguin in snow live in very different places.
"Habitats matter," said Asha.

Plants and animals live in forests, deserts, mountains, oceans, grasslands and ponds. Each place is a habitat that gives food, water and shelter.
Living things have features that suit their habitat. Cactus stems store water in deserts, and fish have gills for water.
If a habitat is damaged by cutting forests or pollution, many plants and animals lose their home.

problem.en: Why does a cactus survive in a desert?

text.en: It has thick stems that store water.
Its leaves are spines, which lose little water.
So it survives with little rain.

prompt.en: A friend says every animal can live in every habitat. How will you reply?

points.en: A habitat gives food, water and shelter.
